claims.claim: gateway21.pelecard.biz and gateway20.pelecard.biz serve the same Pelecard API; the hostname is not an environment switch. gateway21 is the current gateway generation, gateway20 the older one, and gateway20.pelecard.biz/sandbox is a sandbox UI page rather than a separate API host. Both answer PaymentGW/init, PaymentGW/GetTransaction and PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey identically; whether a call is a test or a live charge is decided by the terminal number and credentials sent.

Only three /PaymentGW paths exist on the Pelecard gateway hosts: PaymentGW/init (create session), PaymentGW/GetTransaction (lookup) and PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey (credential-free validation). Every other /PaymentGW path, including DebitRegular, DebitRegularCancel, Refund, ConfirmDebit, CancelTransaction and GetToken, 302-redirects to an Http404 error page exactly as a deliberately fabricated control path does. There is therefore no refund endpoint under /PaymentGW.

ActionType values: J4 = standard sale (default, money moves), J2 = card validation/registration only (no charge), J5 = authorize now / charge later, J5h = enhanced J5. Money fields use minor units (agorot): Total 9900 = NIS 99.00; the dofinity wrapper documents FirstPayment as in agorot/cents. Currency 1 = ILS (dofinity default $Currency = 1).

claims.claim: Pelecard does NOT HMAC-sign IPN deliveries. The browser-side ConfirmationKey can be forged, so the server-to-server lookup is the only authoritative source. Validation: match the callback ConfirmationKey byte-for-byte to the stored Phase-1 value, then re-call GetTransaction and confirm DebitTotal (the authoritative debited amount, in agorot) and PelecardTransactionId. GetTransaction returns the transaction record (DebitTotal, DebitApproveNumber, Token, TotalPayments, masked card, etc.), not the ConfirmationKey. Dedupe IPNs on PelecardTransactionId (not ParamX). Also covers: 50.00 ₪

claims.claim: Bit wallet constraints: single payment only (no installments), ILS only (Currency 1), per-transaction cap commonly 5,000 NIS (operator-tier-set; higher-tier merchants cleared above), plus a per-merchant monthly cap (~20,000 NIS) and a 10-minute customer time window. Apple Pay is via Pelecard's ClientSecure.js.
claims.raw_snippet: The corresponding switch can be found in the module settings. Restrictions Up to 5000 ILS. Payment via Bit cannot exceed 5,000 shekels. The sum of all payments per month from all customers cannot exceed 20,000 shekels. ILS. Bit only supports payments in shekels. No installments. You can only pay with Bit in one payment. No subscriptions. Bit does not allow you to save your customer card for future charges, so we hide the Bit button for “Subscription” payment links. No payment from Bit balance.

claims.claim: Israeli Consumer Protection Law (חוק הגנת הצרכן, sections 14C-14E) distance-selling refunds: the consumer may cancel within 14 days, the merchant must refund within 14 days of the cancellation notice, and the cancellation fee is capped at 5% of the order value or NIS 100, whichever is lower. Pelecard handles the money; the tax document (credit note / חשבונית זיכוי) is generated by the invoice provider. In addition, customers who are people with disabilities, aged 65 or over, or new immigrants may cancel within 4 months where a conversation took place during the sale, and certain service categories carry shorter windows, so 14 days is not the complete rule.

claims.claim: Pelecard publishes a live public request builder at gateway21.pelecard.biz/services (ServicesRequestBuilder) listing its server-to-server service operations, including Debit Regular Type (J4), the Authorize (J5) family, the Pending (J9) family, token operations, Delete/Reversal operations, ParamX lookups, Broadcast, 3DS initiation and the error-message lookups.

Pelecard's own public request builder script defines the service URLs for its endpoints, confirming the real paths. Verified paths: /services/DebitRegularType, /services/DebitPaymentsType, /services/DebitCreditType, /services/DebitIsracreditType, /services/AuthorizeCreditCard, /services/AuthorizeCreditType, /services/AuthorizePaymentsType, /services/AuthorizeIsracreditCard, /services/PendingRegularType, /services/PendingCreditType, /services/PendingPaymentsType, /services/PendingIsracreditType, /services/ClearPendingByUserKey, /services/ClearPendingByRecordId, /services/ConvertToToken, /services/RetrieveToken, /services/UpdateToken, /services/CheckCreditCardForToken, /services/DeleteTran, /services/DeleteIshur, /services/EmvReversal, /services/EmvFinishDebit, /services/TrxLookUp, /services/CheckGoodParamX, /services/CheckGoodParamXList, /services/CheckGoodParamXEmv, /services/GetTransData, /services/GetCompleteTransData, /services/GetTransDataBeforeBc, /services/GetTransReportDataBeforeBc, /services/Broadcast, /services/GetBroadcast, /services/GetBroadcastsByDate, /services/GetErrorMessageEn, /services/GetErrorMessageHe, /services/GetTerminalName, /services/ResetUserPassword, /services/CreateInvoice, /services/CreateICountInvoice, /services/CreateEZCountInvoice, /Services/Initiate3DSAuthenticationProcess, /Services/InitiateBankTransfer, /PaymentGW/init, /PaymentGW/GetTransaction, /PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey. The corresponding full URLs on the gateway host (for example https://gateway21.pelecard.biz/services/DebitRegularType and https://gateway21.pelecard.biz/services/GetErrorMessageHe) resolve on both gateway hosts. The builder script itself is served at /Scripts/Services/Sandbox.js. All of these are POST endpoints, i.e. POST /PaymentGW/init, POST /PaymentGW/GetTransaction, POST /PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey, POST /Services/Initiate3DSAuthenticationProcess, POST /services/CheckGoodParamX, POST /services/GetTerminalName and POST /services/TrxLookUp. The script defines 57 distinct service URLs in total: 54 under /services/, plus /PaymentGW/GetTransaction, /PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey and /PaymentEnquiry/CreateLink.

The /services surface uses different parameter casing from /PaymentGW: terminalNumber, user, password, shopNumber, creditCard, creditCardDateMmYy, token, total, currency, cvv2, id, authorizationNumber, paramX, userKey, plus eci/xid/cavv for carrying a 3DS2 result into the debit. /PaymentGW uses terminal, Total, Currency, ParamX, ShopNo and TransactionId.

Money fields are in minor units (agorot). Pelecard's own builder sends the same single shekel as total "100" on /services/DebitRegularType and as TotalX100 "100" on PaymentGW/ValidateByUniqueKey, TotalX100 meaning the amount multiplied by 100. This corroborates the agorot convention independently of the dofinity wrapper.

Pelecard publishes the official bilingual message for every status code through /services/GetErrorMessageEn and /services/GetErrorMessageHe, which take only {"ErrorCode":"NNN"} and require NO credentials. A sweep of codes 000-999 on 2026-08-27 returned 254 assigned codes; the rest return the placeholder UnkownError (English) or שגיאה לא ידועה (Hebrew). Verified examples: 000 operation success / עסקה תקינה., 033 invalid credit card. / כרטיס לא תקין., 036 card is expired. / כרטיס פג תוקף., 308 Duplicated transaction. / עסקה כפולה., 425 Double entry / רשומה כפולה., 501 User name and/or password not correct. Please call support team., 502 User password has expired., 506 Token number abnormal. / מספר טוקן לא תקין., 650 3DS process failed / אימות 3ds נכשל, 302 Debit was successful but merchant is not responding / התשלום בוצע אך אתר העסק לא זמין, 301 Session to Pelecard Timed Out, 303 Merchant is not responding, 011 No Approoval From The Clearing Company For This ISO Currency., 012 This ISO Currency is not Allowed for This Credit Card., 401 Number of payments is greater than the maximum number of payments, 402 Number of payments is smaller than a minimum number of payments, 403 Transaction amount is smaller than the minimum amount, 404 Terminal number does not exist., 503 Locked user., 505 Blocked terminal., 507 User is not authorized in this terminal., 508 Expiration date structure invalid. Use MMYY structure only., 620 This card cannot be used for this transaction., 999 Necessary values are missing to complete installments transaction. Codes 660-680 are ISO 20022 bank-transfer statuses (ACCC, ACSC, ACSP, ACTC, ACWC, RCVD, RJCT, PATC, PENDING, ERROR, CAPTCHA fail, ACFC, CANC, INIT), several of which are successes.
